clue.text: Crowd 1 down 17 21 in old Asian city

indicators.note: the cross-reference reads 'back to front', telling us to turn the word for a crowd around

parts.note: a crowd or rabble is a mob
the cross-reference reads 'before the horse': the reversed crowd goes in front of a bay, a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Somewhere in an Asian city of old, a crowd has gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references hide whole phrases: '1 down 17' says 'back to front' and '21' says 'before the horse', the horse being a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai, the Indian port city renamed in 1995.

clue.text: Into action again — war like this is painful

explanation.surface: Returning to battle, as war hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: WAR read in the manner the answer describes gives RAW, which means painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers returning to combat go back to the front line; reading 'war' in reverse spells a word for sore.

clue.text: Speaker introducing a certain bill

indicators.note: the speaker comes first, ushering in what follows

parts.note: the person speaking refers to themself as me
certain means sure

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House bringing in a particular piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Commons Speaker, but it is just the person talking: ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill before parliament is a proposed measure, a piece of draft legislation.

clue.text: Traveller overcome by anxiety — it's a very, very short distance

indicators.note: in a down answer, being overcome means having the other word placed on top

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
a Rom is a Romany, a member of a travelling people

explanation.surface: A traveller beaten by worry over a tiny distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An angstrom is a unit of length of one ten-billionth of a metre, used for atomic distances.

clue.text: Means of keeping in touch during period without company

parts.note: during, as in 'in the night', means in

indicators.note: in its old sense of 'outside', the period word goes around the company abbreviation

parts.note: a school or academic period is a term

explanation.surface: Something that keeps people in contact while a stretch of time passes with no firm involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the period word encloses the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal telephone or speaker system linking rooms of a building.

clue.text: New planet and black hole ultimately almost blue

parts.note: Earth is a planet
ebon is a poetic word for black

indicators.note: means the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A newly found planet and a black hole, described in astronomical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means risqué, not a colour; 'almost blue' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke near the bone is close to indecent, so it is almost smutty.

clue.text: Small flier legate distributed

indicators.note: spread out and dealt round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy handing things out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a small bird.

clue.text: One way to preserve so long a piece of music

parts.note: canning is a way of preserving food
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye, like so long

explanation.surface: A preservation method so lengthy it becomes a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal work for soloists, chorus and orchestra.

clue.text: Old monarch died, put in mortuary that's 18

indicators.note: the letter for died is placed inside the word mortuary
the cross-reference reads 'out of order', signalling the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dead monarch placed in a mortuary.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is OUT OF ORDER: D goes into MORTUARY and the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Tudor was Mary I, Queen of England from 1553 to 1558.

clue.text: What opponents in court regularly do to influence conclusions

definitions.text: What opponents in court regularly do

explanation.surface: Tennis players swapping sides, or someone swaying outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'court' is a tennis court; the second reading takes the phrase literally as altering the final results.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis players switch sides of the net during a match; to alter outcomes is also to alter the finishing points.

clue.text: Pass composer on the outside as driver

indicators.note: says the composer's name sits around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Richard Wagner, the German opera composer
to pass along or proceed is to go

explanation.surface: A composer being overtaken on the outside, as though in a race between drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A waggoner drives a horse-drawn wagon, so he is a driver of an older kind.

clue.text: Presenting inane chatter in front of others, he stupidly is getting priority wrong

parts.note: to present something is to put it forward

indicators.note: inane chatter is senseless, so its letters are scrambled into nonsense

parts.note: in front of means before

indicators.note: the letters of 'others' and 'he' are arranged without sense, as someone acting stupidly would

explanation.surface: Someone talking pointless chatter ahead of everyone else, foolishly getting priorities backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inane' rearranges CHATTER into THECART; 'stupidly' rearranges OTHERS and HE into THEHORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing things in the wrong order, reversing what should come first.

clue.text: Final disaster for some furnishings displayed in window

parts.note: net means final, as in net profit after deductions
'it's curtains' means it is the end, a disaster

explanation.surface: A final calamity strikes some furnishings in a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: Net curtains are sheer drapes hung across a window for privacy.

clue.text: Gold grabbed in robbery that's second in ten years

indicators.note: the gold is seized and held within the robbery word

parts.note: robbery is theft
OR is gold in heraldry
that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Gold seized in a heist, during a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The forties is the decade from 1940 to 1949, a span of ten years.

clue.text: I notably contrived end of Major

definitions.text: I notably contrived end of Major

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged
takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A politician boasting of engineering the downfall of John Major.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was the Conservative Prime Minister defeated in the 1997 election by the Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour leader won the 1997 general election, ending John Major's premiership.

clue.text: 2 11 1 down 17

indicators.note: the cross-reference reads 'back to front', so the cart word is turned around

parts.note: this light begins 'putting the cart', and a cart is a dray, a low flat wagon

explanation.surface: A string of cross-references that read as a puzzle of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Expanded, the clue says 'measure: putting the cart back to front'; '2' is the light MEASURE, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a unit of length of three feet, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Second rather than first, lacking variety

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
rather than means not
one is first

explanation.surface: Coming second instead of first, without variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotone means unvarying in pitch or tone, so dull and lacking variety.

clue.text: Mark in school — 25

indicators.note: this light means turned backwards, so the school's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A grade given in school.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' is RETRORSE, 'turned backwards'. 'Mark' is the verb, as in 'mark my words'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to note it, take heed of it.

clue.text: See 1
Not working as an anagram

explanation.surface: A broken machine, or jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty machine is broken down; an anagram has its letters scrambled from their proper sequence.

clue.text: 25 with locks? That's sweet

indicators.note: this light means turned backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tressed means having locks of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdo turned around, and it's sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert is a sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Scored quickly with pressure before interval at Oval

parts.note: a rest is an interval or pause
an oval shape suggests the letter O

explanation.surface: Runs scored fast under pressure before the break at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here it is simply the letter O; 'Scored' means marked in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction meaning very fast.

clue.text: See 11
See 9
In relation to hearing, everything contained in accusation is false

indicators.note: a false version is a corrupted one, signalling a rearrangement
all that lies within the word, so its first and last letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Concerning a court hearing, every charge in the accusation is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everything contained in' leaves CCUSATIO from ACCUSATION; 'is false' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic means relating to sound or the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Single guy, heartless and unsmiling

parts.note: sole means single or only

indicators.note: the man loses his middle letter, his heart

parts.note: a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A lone man without feeling and with a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and serious, so not smiling.

clue.text: Error set 18 1 down 17

indicators.note: the cross-reference reads 'out of order', so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Cross-references that read as an error put in the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is OUT OF ORDER, rearranging ERRORSET; the definition '1 down 17' is BACK TO FRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrorse is a botanical term for parts bent or pointing backwards.

clue.text: 9 22 in sector for some pages

indicators.note: the cross-reference reads 'change ends', so the first and last letters of the word swap places

explanation.surface: A swap of the extremes within one section, for a few pages.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 22' is CHANGE ENDS: SECTOR with its outer letters exchanged, S and R trading places.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectos are the right-hand pages of an open book, the front sides of leaves.
